links.outcome: Discrimination of original calculator on local data versus published, and after local recalibration
links.effect: Original calculator c-statistic 0.71 (BTH) and 0.61 (PFW) vs 0.80 originally; calibration poor; after refit c-statistics 0.84 and 0.74.
links.quote: This performance was lower than the original calculator's published model discrimination (c‐statistic 0.80), and calibration was poor.

links.outcome: Improvement in discrimination from local tuning methods (intercept, logistic, full refit)
links.effect: Recalibration-in-the-large and logistic recalibration gave minimal improvement; full refit raised c-statistic to 0.84 (BTH) and 0.74 (PFW); refit models had higher net benefit.
links.quote: After refitting new models on each site, BTH's c‐statistic improved to 0.84, and PFW's c‐statistic improved to 0.74 (Figure 1 ).

links.outcome: Performance degradation from population differences between original development cohort and local sites
links.effect: Original model discrimination dropped at both sites (0.71/0.72 BTH, 0.61 PFW vs 0.80) and external validation did not detect population shifts.
links.quote: External validation is used primarily to determine model transportability, but in this case the original model did not detect shifts in differences between our populations and the original calculator's cohort.

links.outcome: Model generalization to new hospital populations
links.effect: Original calculator c-statistics 0.71 and 0.61 at new sites versus 0.80 in the original cohort; recalibration was needed.
links.quote: Model discrimination for each of our cohorts using the original calculator was satisfactory, albeit with lower discriminative ability (c-statistics were 0.71 and 0.61 for BTH and PFW, respectively), compared with the original calculator's cohort (c-statistic 0.80).

links.outcome: Model performance differences across sites with different demographics
links.effect: Original calculator performed worse at PFW (0.61) than BTH (0.72); refit c-statistics 0.84 vs 0.74; site-stratified models needed.
links.quote: Our models demonstrated that differences in baseline risk, case mix, and hospital settings (even a few city blocks apart, as our hospitals are) will alter the performance of a risk prediction model.
